summary: git blame shows who last changed each line of a file and in which commit. Use it to find the commit that explains a line.
notes: Each line starts with a short commit hash. Pass it to git show to see the whole commit.
blame shows the last change only. If a line was edited twice, git log -L 3,3:gradebook.py shows every version.
A ^ before a hash marks the first commit in the history. Lines you have not committed yet show 00000000 and Not Committed Yet.
pitfall: The author in blame is whoever made the commit, which is not always who wrote the idea. Read the commit message before you blame a teammate.
setup_note: Starts with three commits on main. Maya Lopez made the first and last ones. Her teammate Jordan Kim made the middle one.
setup:
cat > gradebook.py <<'EOF'
scores = [88, 92, 79, 95]
average = sum(scores) / len(scores)
print("Average:", average)
EOF

cat > scores.csv <<'EOF'
name,score
Ava,88
Liam,92
Noah,79
Zoe,95
EOF
git add -A && git commit -q -m "Add gradebook script"
git add -A && git -c user.name="Jordan Kim" -c user.email=jordan@example.com commit -q -m "Round the average to one decimal"
git add -A && git commit -q -m "Add Eli's score"
